## Not adopted

### `code-review` — rejected

*mattpocock_skills · `84fdeff` · ruled in round-001-council-consolidation*

Same job as code-review-and-quality. Its two genuinely distinctive rules were absorbed.

### `code-reviewer` — rejected

*The-Claude-Protocol · `af754ef` · ruled in round-008-claude-protocol*

Strictly weaker than our code-review skill: a single haiku pass (code-reviewer.md:5) guarding the most judgment-heavy step while opus goes to scouting and merges; no mode contract, no severity calibration, no bounded fix loop (its re-review loop has no cap), no re-review scope rules. Its one distinctive idea — the reviewer re-runs the implementer's DEMO commands — we deliberately decline: our evidence discipline binds the implementer, and the diff is the evidence.

### `requesting-code-review` — rejected

*superpowers · `44c9b2d` · ruled in round-001-council-consolidation*

The 'ask for a review' half of a two-part protocol; belongs with the rubric it dispatches. Note this merge requires repointing subagent-driven-development's hard reference to code-reviewer.md.

### `subagents-discipline` — deferred

*The-Claude-Protocol · `af754ef` · ruled in round-008-claude-protocol*

The newer variant (2026-01-31) of sk-072: it drops the DEMO/PARTIAL/checklist evidence machinery and adds orchestration wiring — Rule 0 (consume the dispatch context from the bead, stop and ask if missing, templates/skills/subagents-discipline/SKILL.md:8-25) and optional approach logging (:94-107). The evidence rules were already ruled via sk-072; the one distinct idea, a worker-side context obligation mirroring our coordinator-side delegation rule, is deferred. Re-open: a real case of a worker re-investigating what the coordinator already established — then it becomes one bullet in rules/core/01-delegation.md.

### `validate-completion.sh` — rejected

*The-Claude-Protocol · `af754ef` · ruled in round-008-claude-protocol*

TCP's flagship gate, and the strongest single reason to distrust the framework's enforcement claims: it reads .agent_transcript_path — not a documented SubagentStop field — and explicitly approves-and-exits when it is empty (:7, :11), so it fails open; its block shape ({"decision":"block"}) is also undocumented for SubagentStop. Even granting the plumbing, it checks only bookkeeping (worktree exists, tree clean, branch pushed, status inreview, response length) and never test evidence — 'Tests: pass' is a literal template string the worker fills in. Our verification-before-completion is a strictly better specification; the mechanizable subset (epic-close) goes to cr-ghw instead.
